Sasha: Heads-up — CI evals for the new int8 candidate show BLEU regression only when smoothing is enabled. Repro steps below.
Sasha: ```bash
# run failing job locally
python eval_runner.py --model=redwood/m45-int8 --metric=bleu --smoothing=exp --seed=42
```
Sasha: Short summary: same prompt set, fp16 vs int8, smoothing=exp => fp16 BLEU 28.7, int8 BLEU 24.2. Without smoothing numbers match within noise. :thinking_face:
Jordan: @Sasha can you paste the tokenized output for a single failing example (fp16 vs int8)?
Sasha: pasted one below:
```
# fp16 tokens:
['We', 're', '-', 'architect', 'this', '.']
# int8 tokens:
['We', 're-', 'architect', 'this', '.']
```
Sasha: That hyphen merge changes ngram counts used by smoothing code.
Priya: Huh. So the smoothing is applied at the token-ngram level and assumes tokenization is consistent across runs. If quantization changes tokenization (due to logit rounding affecting BPE merge decisions), smoothing can amplify the diff.
Ravi: Another angle — in some examples int8 logits produce equal top-2 scores leading to different tie-breaks in merge steps. That can swap merges for hyphen tokens. We saw identical logits in small vocab subsets earlier.
Priya: Proposed quick fixes: 1) detokenize before computing BLEU (sacrebleu's default uses tokenization heuristics), 2) add an explicit smoothing that operates on detokenized ngrams (char-level fallback), 3) add a CI sanity test asserting tokenization stability for canonical inputs across precisions.
Jordan: I like detokenize first. It's closer to downstream human text quality. Also add a regression test that runs 10 seed variations and asserts BLEU change < 2.0 when switching precision.
Sasha: Config snippet I'll add to eval runner:
```json
{"metric": "bleu", "tokenize": "none", "smoothing_method": "floor", "detokenize_before_metric": true}
```
Sasha: Will open PR with: detokenize step, unit that compares token counts and a small example asserting merges are identical between fp16/int8 or failing loudly with useful diff output.
Ravi: For the long term we should also consider forcing canonical merge tie-breaker in tokenizer when run in CI (deterministic merges based on hash seed) — avoids nondeterminism introduced by minor logit perturbations.
Priya: Also file a follow-up to check BERTScore embedding drift for same cases; embeddings looked near-equal but BERTScore sometimes masked that because of idf weighting.
Jordan: TL;DR: Sasha -> PR to detokenize+floor smoothing + add tokenization stability test. Priya/Ravi -> follow-ups for tokenizer determinism + BERTScore drift investigation.
Sasha: I'll tag the PR as WIP and run smoke on the int8 branch. Leaving a note to @eval-bot to re-run the nightly quant-compare job after merge. :eyes:
eval-bot: queued job quant-compare/nightly (refs: m45-int8) — will report results in #eng-ml once done.
